title: Signature Sync Transparency Log
description: Signature edition: every sync operation is logged to a transparency log — which devices synced, when, what changed (hashes only, never content). The log lets users audit their own sync history and detects anomalous sync activity (a new device syncing everything at 3am). This is a Signature original method.
method: Log (device, time, change hashes) per sync; users review their log; anomaly detection flags unusual patterns.
usage: Show users their sync log; alert on anomalies; investigate promptly.

demo.code:
print('sync log: laptop 10:02 (12 changes), phone 10:05 (12 changes)')
print('unknown device 03:14 full sync -> ANOMALY ALERT')

title: Signature Encrypted CRDT sync
description: Signature edition: CRDTs need to see operations to merge them — but encrypted CRDTs merge ciphertext operations using deterministic encryption or trusted ordering, converging without the sync server reading content. Collaboration with convergence, minus the server's visibility.
method: Encrypt operations deterministically (or order via a blind sequencer); replicas merge ciphertext; convergence preserved.
usage: Accept the metadata leakage consciously (operation counts, sizes); pad where it matters.

demo.code:
print('ops encrypted deterministically; server merges ciphertext')
print('replicas converge; server learned: op count only')

title: Signature Sync integrity verification
description: Signature edition: A malicious server could fork the state (show different versions to different clients) or drop updates. Integrity verification — hash chains, Merkle trees over the log, gossip between clients — detects server misbehavior. CONIKS and Key Transparency do this for key directories; the same idea secures state sync.
method: Hash-chain the update log; clients gossip roots; mismatched roots expose forks; dropped updates break the chain.
usage: Gossip roots out-of-band periodically; treat mismatches as security incidents.

demo.code:
print('client A root: r7f2; client B root: r7f2 (gossip match)')
print('server fork attempt: roots diverge -> DETECTED')

title: Signature Device pairing and provisioning
description: Signature edition: New devices join the sync mesh by pairing: an existing device verifies the new one (QR code, numeric comparison) and provisions the sync keys. Pairing is the trust root — a weak pairing flow lets attackers join the mesh and read everything.
method: Out-of-band verification (QR/numeric); provision keys over the verified channel; the new device syncs ciphertext after.
usage: Make pairing verification mandatory and unskippable; log new device joins.

demo.code:
print('new phone: scan QR from laptop (verified)')
print('keys provisioned; phone syncs ciphertext; join logged + notified')

title: Signature Offline-first secure sync
description: Signature edition: Offline-first means the local replica is primary: edits work without connectivity, sync merges when possible, and encryption never depends on the server being reachable. The security model holds offline — keys are local, ciphertext syncs when it can.
method: Local encrypted replica primary; sync opportunistically; merge on reconnect; keys never require the server.
usage: Design for offline from the start; test the merge-after-long-offline path.

demo.code:
print('offline 3 days: 42 local edits (encrypted at rest)')
print('reconnect: sync, merge, converge — no key ever needed the server')

title: Signature Revocation propagation
description: Signature edition: When a device is lost or a member removed, revocation must propagate to every replica — including offline ones, which learn at next sync. The protocol marks the key dead, rotates, and quarantines data the revoked key touched after the compromise window.
method: Broadcast revocation; rotate keys; offline replicas learn on sync; quarantine post-compromise data for review.
usage: Automate revocation; assume offline devices exist; review quarantined data.

demo.code:
print('device lost -> revocation broadcast, keys rotated')
print('offline laptop syncs next week: learns revocation, re-encrypts')

title: Signature Conflict resolution without decryption
description: Signature edition: When encrypted replicas conflict, the server (or the protocol) must order or merge without seeing content: deterministic timestamps, CRDT semantics on ciphertext, or client-side resolution after sync. The conflict logic operates on metadata and ciphertext structure, never plaintext.
method: Order by HLC timestamps; merge via encrypted-CRDT rules; clients resolve residual conflicts locally after decrypt.
usage: Design the conflict rules before the encryption; test concurrent encrypted edits.

demo.code:
print('concurrent edits: HLC orders them; CRDT merges ciphertext')
print('server resolved conflict having seen: timestamps only')

title: Signature Double Ratchet for sync channels
description: Signature edition: The Signal protocol's Double Ratchet gives sync channels forward secrecy and post-compromise recovery: keys evolve with every message, so a stolen key decrypts little past traffic and future traffic heals. State sync over ratcheted channels survives key compromise gracefully.
method: Ratchet keys per message (DH + symmetric chain); old keys deleted; compromise heals on the next exchange.
usage: Use for sync between mutually distrustful or at-risk devices; the ratchet is the recovery story.

demo.code:
print('message 100: key K100; device stolen at 100')
print('attacker reads ~0 past (deleted) ; future heals at next DH ratchet')

title: Signature Key rotation for shared state
description: Signature edition: Shared-state keys must rotate: members leave, devices are lost, and long-lived keys accumulate risk. Rotation re-encrypts state under a new key and distributes it to current members only — the departed member's key dies with their access. MLS (Messaging Layer Security) standardizes this for groups.
method: Generate new key; re-encrypt state; distribute to current members; revoke old; MLS for group messaging scale.
usage: Rotate on every membership change; schedule periodic rotation; automate it.

demo.code:
print('member leaves -> rotate: state re-encrypted under K2')
print('departed member holds K1: reads nothing new')
